title: Route Refresh Capability for BGP-4
summary: Defines a Border Gateway Protocol capability that lets one BGP speaker ask another to resend its routes. This allows a policy change to take effect without resetting the connection. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: Two routers share road maps. If one changes its rules, it can ask for the maps again without hanging up the phone.

questions: how to re-request bgp routes without reset
subtitle: A BGP capability that lets a router ask its peer to resend its routes without resetting the session.

tldr.problem: BGP-4 had no way to ask a peer to re-advertise its routes. After an inbound policy change, the common workaround was to keep an unmodified copy of all routes from that peer, costing memory and CPU.
tldr.mechanism: Peers advertise a Route Refresh Capability, then either side may send a ROUTE-REFRESH message naming an address family. The receiver re-advertises its Adj-RIB-Out for it.
tldr.outcome: Policy changes can be applied without storing extra copies. The unit metadata says RFC 7313 updates this document.

today: RFC 2918 is a Proposed Standard that is updated by RFC 7313, so read the two together.

sections.title: The Problem with Policy Changes
sections.content:
BGP-4 had no mechanism to dynamically ask a peer to re-advertise its Adj-RIB-Out. When the inbound routing policy for a peer changes, all prefixes from that peer have to be re-examined against the new policy.

The commonly used approach, soft-reconfiguration, stores an unmodified copy of every route from the peer at all times, even though policies change infrequently (the RFC says typically no more than a couple of times a day). That costs additional memory and CPU. RFC 2918 offers an alternative without that cost.
sections.eli5: Instead of keeping a photocopy of every map just in case your rules change, you can ask for a fresh copy when you need one.

sections.title: The Route Refresh Capability
sections.content: A speaker advertises the capability using BGP Capabilities Advertisement, with Capability code 2 and Capability length 0. Advertising it tells the peer that the speaker can receive and properly handle the ROUTE-REFRESH message.
sections.eli5: Before asking, each router says I know how to answer this kind of request.

sections.title: The ROUTE-REFRESH Message
sections.content:
ROUTE-REFRESH is a new BGP message type, Type 5. Its body is one <AFI, SAFI> pair: a 16-bit Address Family Identifier, an 8-bit Reserved field and an 8-bit Subsequent Address Family Identifier. The meaning and encoding follow the Multiprotocol Extensions for BGP-4 (RFC 2858).

The Reserved field should be set to 0 by the sender and ignored by the receiver.
sections.eli5: The request says which kind of map you want, and nothing else.

sections.title: Operation
sections.content:
A speaker may send ROUTE-REFRESH only if it has received the capability from its peer, and the <AFI, SAFI> should be one that the peer advertised at session establishment through capability advertisement.

If a speaker receives a message with an <AFI, SAFI> it did not advertise, it ignores the message. Otherwise it re-advertises the Adj-RIB-Out for that <AFI, SAFI> to the peer, based on its outbound route filtering policy. The security section says the extension does not change the underlying security issues.
sections.eli5: You may only ask if the other router said it can answer, and only for map types it agreed to share.

fields.name: Res.
fields.desc: Reserved; sender sets to 0, receiver ignores.
